tasks.title: is_even
tasks.objective:
Write only Python, no markdown.

Implement:

def is_even(n: int) -> bool

Return True when n is an even integer and False otherwise. Zero counts as even. Negative even numbers are even.
tasks.holdout_test:
assert is_even(4) is True
assert is_even(5) is False
assert is_even(0) is True
assert is_even(-2) is True
assert is_even(-3) is False
print('ok')

tasks.title: reverse
tasks.objective:
Write only Python, no markdown.

Implement:

def reverse_string(s: str) -> str

Return the characters of s in reverse order. An empty string returns an empty string.
tasks.holdout_test:
assert reverse_string('ab') == 'ba'
assert reverse_string('') == ''
assert reverse_string('abc') == 'cba'
assert reverse_string('a') == 'a'
print('ok')

tasks.title: merge_sorted
tasks.objective:
Write only Python, no markdown.

Implement:

def merge_sorted(a: list, b: list) -> list

Both inputs are already sorted ascending. Return one sorted list containing every element from both, keeping duplicates. Either input may be empty.
tasks.holdout_test:
assert merge_sorted([1, 3], [2]) == [1, 2, 3]
assert merge_sorted([], [1]) == [1]
assert merge_sorted([1, 2], []) == [1, 2]
assert merge_sorted([], []) == []
assert merge_sorted([1, 1], [1]) == [1, 1, 1]
assert merge_sorted([1, 5], [2, 6]) == [1, 2, 5, 6]
print('ok')

tasks.title: levenshtein
tasks.objective:
Write only Python, no markdown.

Implement:

def levenshtein(a: str, b: str) -> int

Return the Levenshtein edit distance between the two strings: the minimum number of single-character insertions, deletions or substitutions needed to turn a into b.
tasks.holdout_test:
assert levenshtein('kitten', 'sitting') == 3
assert levenshtein('', 'abc') == 3
assert levenshtein('abc', '') == 3
assert levenshtein('abc', 'abc') == 0
assert levenshtein('flaw', 'lawn') == 2
print('ok')

tasks.title: scratch_parser
tasks.objective:
Write only Python, no markdown. Single module, multiple functions.

Implement:

def parse_pair(s: str) -> tuple
    'a=1' becomes the pair ('a', 1), with the value converted to int.

def format_pair(k, v) -> str
    The inverse: ('a', 1) becomes 'a=1'.

The two functions must round-trip.
tasks.holdout_test:
assert parse_pair('a=1') == ('a', 1)
assert format_pair('a', 1) == 'a=1'
assert parse_pair(format_pair('k', 42)) == ('k', 42)
assert parse_pair('zz=0') == ('zz', 0)
print('ok')
